description: Conformance vectors for the EVM-log anchor-pointer mechanism requested by Tetsurohhori (aos-standard/catalog) in aeoess/agent-governance-vocabulary#217: {chain, contract, tx, log_index, height} resolved against a live EVM node, with anchored_digest checked against the indexed topic of the Anchored event at that exact log position. No proof blob is pinned -- for EVM, the chain itself is the proof, queried live. These vectors carry no code: an independent reader is expected to resolve each one against a real Base-mainnet (and, for two negatives, Arbitrum-mainnet) RPC endpoint.

mechanism.event_signature: Anchored(bytes32 indexed ref, address indexed anchoredBy, uint256 timestamp)
mechanism.contract: AnchorRegistry, permissionless, single function anchor(bytes32 ref). Canonical CREATE2 address, identical on Base (8453), Arbitrum One (42161) and Ink (57073): 0x49fEcA52bC634a9Ab773226D16619deC547794aa.
mechanism.resolution: Fetch the transaction receipt for `tx` on `chain`. Find the log in receipt.logs whose logIndex == `log_index`. Verify: log.address == `contract` (case-insensitive); log.blockNumber == `height`; log.topics[0] == event_topic0; log.topics[1] == `anchored_digest` (case-insensitive). anchoredBy (topics[2]) and timestamp (data) are informational, not checked by this vector set.
mechanism.note_on_proof: No `proof` field is required for this mechanism -- the live receipt lookup above IS the proof. A vector may carry `proof: null` to confirm a reader does not wrongly require it.

primary_source.note: The positive vector is a real anchor, independently re-verified against eth_getTransactionReceipt on https://mainnet.base.org on 2026-10-23 (not taken from any script printout or prior write-up). It anchors the gt-v2.1 release-statement digest that AXES (magentixai, axes#18) requested in axes#3 as a custody record -- the anchored_digest below is a byte-exact match against the calldata AXES supplied, confirmed independently before this file was built. The preimage behind that digest is AXES's write_once_store construction, out of scope here: this vector set tests only the EVM anchor-pointer mechanism, not the digest's own preimage spec.

vectors.description: Baseline: the real gt-v2.1 custody anchor, all fields exactly as returned by eth_getTransactionReceipt. No proof field.
Same real anchor; contract address given lowercase, no EIP-55 checksum casing. EVM addresses are case-insensitive -- a reader that requires exact checksum casing on this field is over-strict.

Same real anchor; tx hash given with an uppercase hex body. Hex is case-insensitive -- a reader that lowercases before RPC lookup (or treats the RPC's own case-insensitivity as sufficient) should still resolve this.

Same real anchor, with an explicit `proof: null` field present. Confirms proof is optional-by-mechanism for EVM (the chain query is the proof) and must not be required or treated as a failure when absent or null.

Real chain, real confirmed tx -- but `contract` names a different real, live contract on Base (USDC: 0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913, 1852 bytes of deployed code, confirmed via eth_getCode 2026-10-23), not AnchorRegistry. The log at log_index 59 of this tx is emitted by AnchorRegistry's address, not the declared contract.

Correct tx hash, but `chain` declares Arbitrum One (eip155:42161) instead of Base. This exact tx hash does not exist on Arbitrum -- confirmed live via eth_getTransactionReceipt on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc on 2026-10-23, result: null. AnchorRegistry is deployed at the same address on both chains, which is exactly why the chain field must be checked and not inferred from the contract address alone.
Chain id given as a bare number without the CAIP-2 'eip155:' namespace. Format-level rejection, not a chain-resolution failure -- a reader should reject this before attempting any RPC call.
Syntactically well-formed 32-byte tx hash that does not correspond to any transaction on Base. Confirmed live via eth_getTransactionReceipt on https://mainnet.base.org on 2026-10-23, result: null.

Real, confirmed Base tx (status 0x1), same block (52987624) as the positive vector -- but its `to` is 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000015 (the L1Block predeploy), not AnchorRegistry, and it emits no logs at all. Confirmed live via eth_getTransactionReceipt on 2026-10-23.

Real tx, real contract, real digest -- but `log_index` is 0. This tx's receipt has exactly one log, at logIndex 59 (0x3b); there is no log at index 0 belonging to this tx. (This tx has only one log in total, confirmed live 2026-10-23, so there is no second real log to point at instead -- log_index 0 stands in for 'declared index does not resolve to this tx's Anchored log.')
Real tx, but `height` declares 52986624 (1000 blocks earlier -- itself a real, already-mined Base block, not a nonsense number) instead of the tx's actual block, 52987624.

Real tx, but `height` declares 999999999999 -- far beyond Base's current chain head (52987624 at anchor time; ~53007902 when this file was built, 2026-10-23). Distinct failure class from -height-001: here the declared height cannot yet be real at all, versus a real-but-wrong block.
Real tx/contract/chain/height/log_index, but `anchored_digest` has its last hex nibble flipped (…de88299 -> …de88298) relative to the real topics[1] value.

Harder variant of -digest-001: `anchored_digest` is not nonsense, it is itself a real, validly anchored 32-byte ref in the same AnchorRegistry contract -- just from a different anchor (giskard09/dapr-history-anchor, tx 0x8702287dca01fb5faa76ec8c95b67322d2f685e634747ba9177082bd72c50a39, Base block 48545657, re-verified live via eth_getTransactionReceipt on 2026-10-23). It is not the ref emitted by THIS tx's log. Tests that a reader checks the digest against the specific (tx, log_index) pointed to, not against 'any ref this registry has ever anchored.'

omitted_by_design.reorg_finality: No reorg/finality vector is included in this draft. A static JSON fixture cannot encode 'chain state changed between read and verify' -- that is a property of how a live reader handles confirmations/finality tags on its own RPC calls, not something a fixed (chain, tx, log_index, height, digest) tuple can represent. Flagging this as a possible follow-on if useful, not building it speculatively.
